name: Solar ignition
summary: Sunlight focused to a point that smokes — no fuel, no consumables, and it works with things that are not lenses.

steps.text: Set the tinder on a stable base out of the wind, with a dark surface if you have one.
steps.why: Dark absorbs; pale reflects. Char cloth ignites under a lens far faster than dry grass for exactly this reason.

steps.text: Move the lens toward and away from the tinder until the bright spot is as SMALL and as SHARP as you can make it — a hard point, not a bright blur.
Hold it dead still. Brace your wrists against your knees; a hand-held wobble spreads the spot and it never gets there.

WATER BOTTLE: fill a clear smooth bottle, hold it upright, and use the curved side as a cylindrical lens. It focuses to a line rather than a point — a clear round bottle works far better than a ribbed or crumpled one.
ICE LENS: shape clear (not cloudy) ice into a thick disc, thin at the edges and fat in the middle, and polish it with the warmth of your hands.
REFLECTOR: a parabolic headlight or flashlight reflector focuses to a point about where the bulb sat. Push the tinder into the bulb hole from behind.
When it smokes, keep the focus on it until there is a live coal, then transfer to the tinder bundle.

verify: A smoking black spot that keeps growing after you take the light off it.
If the spot is bright but nothing happens, it is not small enough — or the sun is too low.
limits: NO SUN, NO FIRE. It is useless at night, under overcast, in haze and in deep forest shade, and it weakens sharply within a couple of hours of sunrise and sunset.
It gives you a coal, not a flame — the tinder bundle still does the rest of the work.
It needs a genuinely clear focusing medium. Cloudy ice, scratched plastic and coloured bottles all fail.
cautions: Never look at the focused spot; it is bright enough to hurt your eyes.
A lens left in the sun in a pack has started fires unattended. Store it covered.
